summary:
We built the Cross-Planetary Terrestrial Analog Discovery Engine, an end-to-end geospatial pipeline, FastAPI backend, and interactive 3D/2D WebGIS platform that discovers and explains Earth analog sites for 8 fixed Moon (Artemis) and Mars exploration targets.

Instead of comparing distorted latitude/longitude grids or opaque single similarity scores, our engine projects orbital data onto body-specific Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area (LAEA) metric grids across 5 physical domains (topography, mineralogy, thermal/illumination, granular/aeolian, volatiles/subsurface) and 5 resolution octaves (30–480 m/px). Optimized C++20/OpenMP kernels compute local Wasserstein-1 quantile and texture similarity, a 150 km novelty mask suppresses already over-studied sites, and a breakdown synthesizer reports both physical divergences and matching Artemis/Mars engineering tests.

This helps mission planners quickly identify diverse, mission-relevant terrestrial field testbeds for rover mobility, ISRU, subsurface robotics, and polar hazard avoidance.
details:
The engine evaluates 14 curated Earth sites (10 discovery candidates such as Morocco's Anti-Atlas and Jebel Saghro, Mistastin Lake, Qaidam Basin, Afar Depression, Undara Lava Tubes, Lut Desert, Tanezrouft, Yakutia, and Kumtagh + 4 known-analog calibration controls) against 8 fixed Moon and Mars reference targets (112 site-target pairs).

  1. Ingest & LAEA Standardization (pipelines/, processor/): Stages 512×512 grids—streaming live Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and MODIS/Aqua MYD11A1 COGs where supported, alongside explicitly tagged calibrated geophysical fallbacks—then projects them to body-radius spherical LAEA grids and builds 5 Gaussian-anti-aliased octaves (30, 60, 120, 240, 480 m/px) in .ptile binary files.
  2. C++20 Local-Distribution Engine (OptiAlgo/ & BestAlgo/): Zero-copy mmap C++20/OpenMP modules compute z-scored physical channel Wasserstein-1 quantile distances ([Q10..Q90]) and texture-energy mismatches across sliding windows (31×31 down to 7×7), verified against Python references (RMSE < 1e-7, SSIM 1.000000, 10×–41× speedup).
  3. Fusion & Mission Mapping (fusion/): Combines domain scores, filters scale invariance, applies 150 km GeoJSON known-analog suppression (known_analogs_mask.geojson), emits physical breakdown flags (gravity, pressure, radiation, thermal floor, biosphere NDVI), and maps matches to Artemis/Mars hardware test protocols.
  4. API & Interactive Frontends (app/, analog-discovery-engine/, Frontend2/): FastAPI serves ranked JSON, RGBA PNG heatmaps, GeoJSON buffers, and a built-in Leaflet + Chart.js dashboard, paired with two React + Three.js frontends that wrap equirectangular surface textures onto 3D spheres and export standalone HTML/print reports.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Metric Fairness: Eliminates lat/lon distortion across Earth (6371.0 km), Moon (1737.4 km), and Mars (3389.5 km).
  • Scientific Honesty: Surfaces why an analog breaks down physically (e.g., 1g vs 0.165g or biosphere overprint) rather than hiding limits behind one number.
  • Discovery Beyond Crowded Sites: The 150 km novelty mask highlights under-explored field testbeds outside Atacama, Mojave, or Iceland.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Cross-Planetary Physics & Dual-Mode Biosphere Handling: Included low-angle solar illumination proxies (sin(slope)·cos(aspect)) for lunar polar craters and separate Moon vs. Mars NDVI thresholds (BIOSPHERE_OVERPRINT vs. ASTROBIOLOGY_EXTREMOPHILE_ANALOG).
  • Per-Channel Provenance: Every tile sidecar explicitly tracks REAL_ORBITAL_COG vs. CALIBRATED_FALLBACK so fallback profiles are never mistaken for measured orbital data.
  • Client Performance: Replaced a 21.1 MB 3D .glb Earth model with lightweight UV-mapped surface textures on THREE.SphereGeometry.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages: Python 3, C++20 (OpenMP, mmap, ASAN/UBSan), JavaScript/JSX, GLSL shaders, HTML/CSS, SQL.
  • Backend & Science: FastAPI, Uvicorn, HTTPX, NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, Pillow, sqlite3.
  • Frontend & GIS: React 18, Vite 5, Three.js (0.169.0), Leaflet 1.9.4 + OpenStreetMap, Chart.js 4.4.0.
  • Dev & Verification: g++, Node.js (node --test), Python unittest, Git/GitHub, Linux / Windows WSL2.
